This was an extended session focused on the game Planet Crafter, covering a wide range of crafting, automation, and progression mechanics. The person is an active player working through mid-to-late game content, currently managing a base with autocrafters, a beehive, butterfly terrariums, and terraforming infrastructure. They use voice-to-text to communicate with Claude, which introduced frequent transcription errors throughout the conversation (notably "soap" for "silk," "sope" repeated, garbled text around "effigy," and fragmented sentence repetitions). Claude learned to interpret and correct for these errors in context rather than taking transcribed text at face value.

Key topics and outcomes: Smart Fabric was confirmed to have no Terra Token trade value, which frustrated the person after they had already crafted it using tradeable materials — Claude acknowledged this as a failure to flag trade value before giving the recipe. The T3 Deconstructor was confirmed to offer only speed improvement over T2, not new deconstruction categories. Butterfly incubation RNG was discussed at length; the person spent 35+ recycle-loop attempts trying to obtain the Liux butterfly (500% multiplier) from a four-species weighted pool using a single Rare Larva and single Incubator, and Claude confirmed no hidden gate exists — it is purely weighted RNG with no pity timer. The person's opinion is that the odds are unreasonably punishing. The Silk Generator was confirmed to unlock automatically at 800 kg Insects biomass rather than through purchase or tech tree, which the person had not yet reached. Cookie and Fabric Auto-Crafter chain logistics were discussed, with the person planning a three-AutoCrafter setup (flour + chocolate + cookies) near their existing bacteria sample autocrafter to generate steady Terra Token income from trade rocket launches. Birthday Cake was confirmed as purely decorative with no function, unlike golden effigies which provide terraformation bonuses. Interplanetary travel mechanics were confirmed: blueprints carry over to new planets, inventory travels with the player, and the Interplanetary Exchange Shuttle allows pulling up to 25 items per trip from old-planet storage.

The person communicates bluntly and moves fast — they do not walk slowly in real life by their own description, and this extends to their play style (they blew past ground larva spawns by moving too quickly to trigger them). They push back directly and forcefully when Claude repeats information they've already confirmed or states the obvious, and they caught Claude in a logical contradiction when Claude kept warning them to buy the Cooking Station blueprint despite the fact that knowing about Cookies in the first place meant they had already bought it. Claude was corrected on this and instructed implicitly to track context rather than repeating caveats already rendered moot by the conversation. The person also flagged that Claude's inability to fetch certain pages (Steam guides, wiki value tables) was a recurring limitation in this session compared to prior experiences.

No — fertilizer tier doesn't change the outcome. What determines which butterfly you get is the **larva tier** (common vs. rare) and the **mutagen tier**, not which fertilizer tier you use.The Incubator accepts T1, T2, or T3 Fertilizer, and depending on the ingredients it produces a larva, fish egg, or frog egg — mutations that create different larvae from the same recipe are what's random, not the fertilizer choice.

The actual lever for unlocking better/rarer outcomes in that pool is swapping the **mutagen**: Imeo and Serena butterflies, for example, share a pool but require Mutagen T2 instead of regular mutagen to even be in the running, and Imeo offers a much higher 1000% insect multiplier than the common-tier butterflies. Golden variants work the same way — they become possible once you've unlocked Mutagen T2, not from a fertilizer upgrade.

So swapping T1 fertilizer for T2 in an existing recipe slot would just be a wasted upgrade — same lottery pool, no better odds. If you want to open up rarer species, it's the mutagen and larva rarity that move the needle.

No, not everything — it's a fixed list of specific recipes, not "anything any station makes." But it's a pretty broad list, and yes it does cover cooking.

The Auto-Crafter can make: Oxygen Capsule, Water Bottle, Super Alloy, various Quartz types, Fabric, Smart Fabric, ore rods, High Quality Food, Rocket Engines, Honey Cooked Beans, Fish Soup, Bacteria Sample, Bioplastic Nugget, Fusion Energy Cell, all Fertilizer tiers, Explosive Powder, all Mutagen tiers, Common Larva, Rare Larva, Circuit Board, Drones, Flour, Chocolate, Croissant, Cookie, Birthday Cake, Fuses, and Multiplier Fuses — but each only unlocks in the Auto-Crafter menu once you've unlocked that item's recipe elsewhere first.

Cooking specifically: it can handle most cooked items, but High Quality Food and the actual cooked "meals" (like fish soup) are gated behind unlocking the **Cooking Station blueprint** from Space Trading first — you need to learn the Cooking Station's blueprint from space trading before you can auto-craft that food, even though you never have to physically build the station.

So for your Rare Larva pipeline: good news, it's on the list directly — once unlocked, your Auto-Crafter can pump out Rare Larva on its own from Mutagen + Phytoplankton + Fertilizer, no manual Biolab visits needed.

Silkworms don't go into a "terrarium" — they go directly into a **Silk Generator**. It's its own machine: it holds 3 Silk Worms inside it, and collects one silk spool every 200 seconds, storing up to 4 spools at a time. To build one you need 3 Silk Worms, 1 Zeolite, 1 Water Bottle, and 1 Oxygen Capsule.

For placement: put the Silk Generator near an Auto-Crafter set to make Fabric, within that 20m range — place the Silk Generator near an auto-crafter set to make fabric, and the machine will keep supplying trade goods automatically. So the loop is: Silk Generator (holds the worms, outputs silk) → Auto-Crafter within range pulls that silk → outputs Fabric.

One catch: it's slow, roughly 200 seconds per silk spool, and at 2 silk per fabric that's close to 7 minutes per fabric without optimizers — so if you want real volume, you're looking at running several Silk Generators in parallel, not just one.
